ChainLink 0.3.699

A much faster start, a cleaner iPhone, and printable reports that finally look the same wherever you make them.

Please re-download once

If your copy stopped offering updates recently, it can't fetch this one either. An expired access key inside older builds switched the updater off silently. Re-download ChainLink once from this link, drag it to Applications, and you're permanently back on automatic updates. Your data is completely untouched. Builds from 0.3.686 onward contain nothing that can expire, so this can't happen again.

It starts up fast now

The "Setting things up…" message used to sit on screen for the best part of a minute on a large library. It now clears in a couple of seconds.

Four separate causes, all measured rather than guessed: a hard-coded minimum display time the message couldn't leave before; the message waiting on iCloud's background chatter even when your whole library was already on disk; an awaited Strava network call sitting on the launch path; and breakthrough analysis holding the message while it ran. None of them made the app do anything useful — they just made it say it was busy.

Printable reports

Reports were losing 56pt of page width to a preview-only margin that was never meant to reach the PDF, so tables squeezed and text wrapped raggedly. Fixed. Reports made on an iPhone were also being rendered oversized and clipped — the whole method column of the Bike Fit sheet was falling off the right edge — and they came out on more pages than the same report made on a Mac. A report now looks identical whichever device made it.

iPhone: more room, less repetition

  • Overview — the four metric cards become one Today strip (Form · Fitness · Recovery), plus a compact "Where you're at" block that links through to Rides, Training and Fitness. Fewer cards, same information.
  • Wellness — your recovery score appeared three times on one screen; now once. Smaller hero ring, so the status and advice have room to read properly.
  • Wrapping fixes — long event names, the peak-power grid, the body-metrics row and the planned-ride row no longer wrap or crush.
  • Connection dots only appear when something is actually wrong.

Also

  • Coach insights are generated when you're looking at them rather than at every launch.
  • Bike builds sync properly across devices, and can be exported and shared as a file.
  • Public holidays are respected when generating a plan; test sessions schedule themselves.

ChainLink 0.3.687

A more reliable update system — plus everything from 0.3.684.

Updates you can trust

ChainLink's built-in updater has been rebuilt to need no credentials at all — the update feed and the downloads are now plain public files. If a download ever fails, you'll see a clear error instead of silence, and nothing that expires can ever switch your updates off again.

If your copy stopped offering updates recently: that was a one-time fault on our side (an expired access key in older builds). Re-download ChainLink once from your original invite link, drag it to Applications, and you're permanently back on automatic updates — your data is untouched.

Recently added (0.3.684)

  • Modules — Settings → Modules lets you switch off the parts of ChainLink you don't use, per device. Data stays safe and synced.
  • Share bike builds — export a build as a file for a friend; import theirs from the Bikes page.
  • Smarter plans — public holidays respected automatically, self-scheduling ramp/CP tests, honest session completion, no phantom workouts.
  • Pull to refresh with a stretching dotted indicator, and a faster app throughout (shared power curve, lighter Rides page).

A note about Strava

As of 30 June 2026, Strava requires an active Strava subscription for the API access ChainLink's Strava connection uses. Syncing through Garmin Connect is unaffected and remains recommended.
